title: Comparison: State Executive vs Union Executive

blocks.content: The Governor is not an employee of the Central Government; it is an independent constitutional office.

rows: Appointed by the President of India
Can pardon death sentences and court-martial (Article 72)
Cannot pardon death sentences or court-martial (Article 161)

items: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V deal with the Union Executive, while Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI deal with the State Executive.
The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence even if a state law prescribes it, but can suspend, remit, or commute it.
The Attorney General is appointed under Article 76, whereas the Advocate General for the State is appointed under Article 165.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Union Executive consists of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and Attorney General of India.
The State Executive consists of the Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers, and Advocate General for the State.
While the President is elected indirectly by an electoral college, the Governor is appointed directly by the President of India.
There is no constitutional position of Vice-Governor in the states, unlike the office of the Vice-President at the Centre.
Pardoning powers of the President extend to court-martial sentences and death sentences, whereas the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence.
